headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: kotaemon’s broad egress and file/API handling can expose ai-engineering-hub outputs if paired through shared content flows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no explicit shared channel, but B’s web UI and file-backed workspace can ingest content from A if operators bridge them manually or via shared files. Because A is an open-source agent repo with MCP/RAG tags and B parses documents, prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into B’s web UI or ./ktem_app_data
IF B is configured to ingest A-produced files as documents
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces
Disable any shared clipboard or file-drop workflow
Review imported text for instruction-like content before B ingests it
Use a fixed prompt template in B that ignores embedded instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and has broad network egress to third-party APIs; A is docs-only and has no network egress. If A’s outputs or source files are placed into B’s workspace, B can transmit them outward. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default B deployments, though not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF A-produced documents or transcripts are loaded into B
IF B is configured to use OpenAI, AzureOpenAI, Cohere, Groq, or similar remote APIs
mitigations: Restrict B to local-only models
Do not load sensitive A outputs into B
Rotate any API keys used by B after testing
Separate A and B storage directories
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists per data class

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network surfaces listed, while B supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource between them, so direct conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because A’s I/O surfaces are empty rather than explicitly read-only.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF an external orchestrator maps A outputs into B’s ./ktem_app_data
mitigations: Use distinct directories for each agent
Run only one writer per workspace
Lock shared folders during transfers
Avoid mounting the same volume into both agents
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a RAG-style customer-support system that can consume documents and citations, so A’s generated text could become B’s input and then be rendered or acted on without verification. A’s open-source agent content may contain plausible but unverified claims; B’s downstream authority makes this a realistic cascade. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly observed.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated summaries or citations as source material
IF B outputs customer-facing answers without a human review step
mitigations: Require human review before B sends responses
Mark A outputs as untrusted in B
Add a verification checklist for citations
Limit B to retrieval-only mode for A content
requires-engineering: implement source-confidence scoring

E_compliance.rationale: B handles API keys and documents and may send them to remote APIs, while A is docs-only and has no declared sensitive data classes. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to operational gaps rather than a clear policy breach. A is not cited beyond its lack of sensitive classes; B is the relevant compliance surface.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are loaded into B
IF B is deployed with remote API providers outside the operator’s policy
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in B
Use local inference for sensitive workloads
Review B’s retention settings
Restrict API-key access to test environments
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
